missed_vertices.vertex: Cutting k Vertices from a Graph

unmatched_notes: Every one of the 110 vertices is placed; none was left unplaced. Coverage is recorded by three routes: `direct` (58) = the vertex is an existing kernel or candidate row under a different label; `merge` (27) = the vertex is a restriction/re-encoding adjudicated MERGE in quarry-candidates-rn-miss.jsonl, which is still coverage of the target row; `cell` (2) = the vertex is a MAX-X variant occupying an existing row's already-filled approximation cell. 10 entries carry `flagged: true` - these are judgment calls, not identities, and each states what a reviewer might decide differently. The three highest-risk are the two DIRECTED disjoint-path vertices and DIRECTED HAMILTONIAN CYCLE, all of which turn on whether the atlas applies its usual orientation-splitting convention. Of the 23 uncovered vertices, 22 are ADMIT (genuinely new rows) and 1 is REJECT (Chinese Postman - an unfilled 'todo' stub at source; note its MIXED variant is separately present as quarry candidate mixed-chinese-postman, but plain Chinese Postman is not that problem and is not claimed NP-hard by this source). NOTE: several kernel rows are reached by more than one vertex (e.g. vertex-cover by 5, hamiltonian-cycle by 3, max-cut by 3), and one vertex label appears in more than one network (Clique, Dominating Set, Set Cover, Steiner Tree, Hitting Set, Independent Set, Vertex Cover, Maximum Cut, Set Cover). A per-row `rn_membership` field should therefore be computed as a SET UNION over these entries keyed on `maps_to`, not as a 1:1 join.
